step: 5c of 8: plate re-picks after the segments v01 contact sheet (intro_10, bridge2_01, closing_01)
method: contact sheets of all five masters (1 frame / 15 s) plus single-frame checks at each pick (/private/tmp/owb_comp/sheets/cands.jpg). Each plate is a ~6 s window from the film's own passed cut, starting at `at` (seconds in the master). The builder lays one plate per spoken line from the VO's Scribe word times (vo_compilation_v01/stt/), 4-6 s each, ~0.4 s xfade, lanczos to 1080p30 on 019/007/005. A plate may carry `windows` instead of one `film`/`at`: the line is split at the VO gap before the window's `from` words (Scribe times).
rules_checked: intro: no plate from the first 30 s of its own film
no plate within 10 s of the film's own out point or of the stretch next to the bridge it sits in
no master window used more than twice across the compilation (picture_qa)
no chapter cards or title cards from the films (007 @345 is a card: rejected)
Orbit only where the film already had him (005 plates are Orbit-heavy; picks avoid him where possible)

plates.line: Nothing you can see in the night sky is permanent.
Not Saturn's rings.
Not the Moon, where it hangs tonight.
plates.what: Earth with the Moon beside it

plates.line: Not even the stars.
Saturn's rings are raining into the planet right now.
plates.what: bright ring detail (verify at full size)

plates.line: The Moon drifts away from us by about three point eight centimetres every year.
plates.what: laser ranging beam on the lunar surface

plates.line: Our galaxy is heading for a meeting with Andromeda.
And every star will one day go out, even the very last one.
So how long does each of them have? That's this film. Five stories, one countdown.
We start with the shortest clock ... about ten trillion years from now.

windows.what: 019's antique clock face, slow push-in (240-247.9 clean)
nebula field: a star flares and goes dark (172-179.9 clean, no Orbit)

plates.repick: v01 005@345 ran into Orbit on a molecule-diagram wall at ~347 s (diagram FAIL risk, off the line)

plates.line: Every one of those clocks is still ticking. First, the rings.
So the rings have somewhere between a hundred and three hundred million years. A blink, for Saturn.
Closer to home, something else is leaving, far more slowly. Every year, the Moon moves a little further away.
plates.what: Moon over Earth (second and last use of this window)

plates.line: The Moon lets go a few centimetres at a time.
plates.what: full Moon over the sea (plan fallback; second and last use of this window)
plates.repick: v01 013@120 was the Moon-forming debris impact, not Earth-Moon

plates.line: But the biggest change coming to our sky ... billions of years away.
plates.what: Andromeda small and far in a dark field

plates.line: When galaxies collide, almost every star sails through untouched.
But no star lasts forever on its own. The biggest end in an explosion, and leave behind something so dense that a teaspoon of it would weigh as much as a mountain.
That's how the biggest stars end: fast, and violently.
plates.what: white star (second and last use of this window)

plates.line: The smallest stars do the opposite ... long after every other star has gone out.
plates.what: starfield / nebula (005 sheet tile 10-11; verify no Orbit, else 005 @165)

plates.line: So that's the countdown. The Moon ... ten trillion years from now.
plates.overlay: code_graphic_owbcomp_timeline_close (J0207), marker 3 + tick, whole timeline reads sound-off

windows.what: laser ranging beam on the lunar surface (second and last use of this window)
ringed gas giant with a far star (275.2-283.0 clean, no Orbit)
burning world in a nebula shrinking to a dim ember (290.8-299 clean)

plates.repick: v01 005@470 ran onto Orbit with constellation linework and sat within 20 s of 005's 488.05 out point; 005@275 alone was 0.3 s short of the line, so the line splits three ways

plates.line: Every clock in the sky is running. And right now, we get to see all of them at once.
plates.what: moonlit sea, today's night sky (from 013's trimmed outro, so not a repeat)
plates.hold: 2-3 s past the last word, then fade
